title: If explanation must end somewhere, why cannot it end with a contingent brute fact?
Why could the independent ground not be a brute contingent existent?
The remaining dispute is whether the exercise itself requires a further contrastive ground.
Asking for another ground can sound like counting the collection twice.
This is one application of the general concept of a brute fact.
If inexplicable means that no sufficient explanation exists, the reason simply repeats the definition of a brute fact.
Every instance of contingent existence has a sufficient explanation for its actuality.
